column1: # Vanilla 26.1.2 entity metadata (set_entity_data) slots, per entity type,
# measured from the server's own sends — not extracted from the jar.
# Why the instrument is the capture and not the jar: the slot indices are
# per-class code (defineSynchedData), so a jar grep cannot say which slots a
# spawn actually emits or at which index. A console `summon` with one client in
# the world makes the vanilla server enumerate them; the capture reads them
# back through this repo's own SetEntityData decoder, which rejects anything it
# cannot fully consume, so every row here walked to a clean terminator.
#                   (chicken and sheep produced nothing: the summoned creeper
#                   killed the client mid-run) plus a night's natural spawns
#                   fill-in run for chicken, sheep and slime (sizes 1/2/4)
#   bodies-lit      the earlier natural-spawn capture (slime, sheep, cow)
# Widths: 1 = one byte, 4 = four bytes, V = VarInt, ? = width not solved from
# the capture (the walk records the pair and stops — the slot table is the
# deliverable, not the value decode). Serializer ids are the captured wire ids;
# only 0 (byte), 1 (varint), 3 (float) and 7 (item stack) are modelled here.
# --- shared LivingEntity slots (present on every mob kind captured) ---
# index 9, serializer 3, width 4: max health, e.g. slime 4.0/9.0, zombie 20.0
# index 6, serializer 20, width ?: on every fresh spawn (re-sync bodies in
#   bodies-lit omit it), suspected pose; values not decoded
# index 8, serializer 7: the item stack — the slot this server already sends
# serializer 10 (index 8) measured as a fixed 8 bytes across 6 bodies
# The table below is the fresh-spawn union per kind. Shared rows (9/3 and 6/20)
# are listed once per kind for grep-ability; that duplication is deliberate.
